content.page_summary: Guidance on ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) and SGLT2 inhibitors for patients with HFrEF, summarizing trial results and practical recommendations.

ARNI_sacubitril_valsartan.indications: Replace an ACE-I or ARB with sacubitril/valsartan in ambulatory patients with HFrEF who remain symptomatic despite optimal treatment.
ARNI_sacubitril_valsartan.hospital_use: Two studies examined ARNI use in hospitalized patients (including ACE-I-naive); initiation appears safe and reduced subsequent CV death or HF hospitalizations by ~42% versus enalapril.
ARNI_sacubitril_valsartan.practical_requirements: Patients should have adequate blood pressure and an eGFR ≥ 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 before starting. A washout period of at least 36 hours after ACE-I therapy is required to minimize angioedema risk.
benefits_reported: Improvement in symptoms and quality of life
Reduction in incidence of diabetes requiring insulin treatment
May allow reduction in loop diuretic requirement
ARNI_sacubitril_valsartan.adverse_effects: Symptomatic hypotension was reported more commonly compared to enalapril, but clinical benefits persisted.

SGLT2_inhibitors.general_recommendation: Dapagliflozin or empagliflozin are recommended in addition to optimal medical therapy (ACE-I/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA) for patients with HFrEF regardless of diabetes status.

DAPA_HF.population: Ambulatory HFrEF patients (NYHA II–IV) with LVEF ≤40% and required elevated NT-proBNP and eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m2 to enroll.
DAPA_HF.outcomes: Dapagliflozin reduced the primary composite endpoint by 26% (worsening HF or CV death). Reduced all-cause mortality, improved HF symptoms, physical function, and QOL. Benefits seen early and across diabetes status and HbA1c spectrum.

EMPEROR_Reduced.population: Patients with NYHA class II–IV symptoms and LVEF ≤40% (trial included patients with eGFR >20 mL/min/1.73 m2).
EMPEROR_Reduced.outcomes: Empagliflozin reduced the combined primary endpoint of CV death or HF hospitalization by ~25%. Associated with reduced decline in eGFR and improved QOL; not a significant reduction in CV mortality in that trial.

SGLT2_inhibitors.additional_notes: SGLT2 inhibitors have diuretic/natriuretic properties that may reduce congestion and allow loop diuretic dose reduction. Sotagliflozin (combined SGLT1/2 inhibitor) showed reduced CV death and hospitalization in diabetic patients hospitalized with HF.
